study: Independent review of NXDN confidence correction and M17 shared decoder reuse
candidate_source: e174edab plus exact weighted convolution costs, uint32 paths and independent block reset

native_corpus.comparison_scope: Frame log records stripped of wall-clock prefix; exact AMBE payload and per-frame error-field equality, greedy ordered-subsequence and suffix comparison
native_corpus.interpretation: Changed voice totals are consistent with changed CRC-based confirmation timing and audio gating. Shared frame records remain identical. This does not establish greater RF accuracy or intelligibility.

m17_replay.scope: Real native fixture replay with stream audio; identical PCM/log behavior. Not M17 BERT, all M17 modes or RF hardware qualification.

review_conclusion: No new correctness blocker found in the isolated arithmetic and start-reset change. Preserve CRC and confirmation gates; make no blanket weak-signal or speedup claim.
limits: NXDN off-air-derived corpus has known fields, not complete payload truth; added or omitted early voice frames cannot all be classified as correct or false.
Ordered frame-log matches have no consumed-sample index and do not measure synchronization latency or align every repeated traffic frame to RF ground truth.
Short CRC matches can occur by chance; improved weighted cost does not eliminate CRC collisions or prove false-acceptance absence.
M17_STATE_DISPATCH stubs the shared convolution routines; M17_REFERENCE_VECTORS does not directly validate this shared decoder's arithmetic.
M17 fixture retains the same existing LSF and embedded-LSF CRC error lines in both variants.
The shared decoder still uses global state and is not safe for concurrent in-process receivers without additional isolation.
No physical receiver or Android device test was performed.
